substance P decreases membrane conductances in hypothalamic neurons.
SP decreased the membrane ionic conductance of neurons in the guineapig hypothalamus.
substance P decreases membrane conductances in neurons of the hypothalamus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of SP on the spontaneous firing rate and the membrane conductance in the hypothalamic neurons.
the effects of SP on membrane conductance of neurons of the gunea pig hypothalamus.
the effect of substance P (SP) on membrane properties of neurons in the guineapig hypothalamus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SP is an excitatory neurotransmitter for hypothalamic neurons, and that the excitatory actions of this peptide are mediated by a decrease in the membrane conductance.
the SP receptor is coupled to a decrease in membrane permeability.

SP is a potent excitant for neurons in the guaina pig hypothalamus, that this effect is due to the decrease of membrane conductance and that the mechanism of this effect is not mediated by a change in the membrane ionic selectivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SP decreases membrane conductance of neurons of the guanine pig hypothalamus, and that this decrease is due to a decrease in K+ conductance.
SP exerts excitatory actions by decreasing membrane ionic permeabilities in neurons of the hypothalamus.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the effects of SP on the membrane conductance of neurons in the guineapig hypothalamus were not due to the release of Ca2+ from intracellular stores or to the influx of Ca2+ via voltage-dependent calcium channels.
the effects of SP on neurons in the central nervous system may not be limited to the excitatory actions of this peptide on the neurons.
the excitatory action of substance P on neurons in the hypothalamus is mediated by a decrease in ionic membrane permeability, and that this action is not dependent on the influx of calcium ions.
